turns.prompt_text: can aquarium plants take the chlorine out of water
turns.response_html:
No, aquarium plants cannot remove chlorine from water. Chlorine and chloramines are toxic chemicals that must be neutralized with a water conditioner or removed via off-gassing (for chlorine only) before adding water to your tank. While plants absorb nitrates and some heavy metals, they are actually harmed by high chlorine levels, which can damage their delicate tissues.

Would you like me to recommend a specific water conditioner or explain how to off-gas tap water?

turns.prompt_text: how can I remove chlorine from water
turns.response_html:
To remove chlorine from your aquarium water, use one of these three methods:

  • Water Conditioner: Use a product like Seachem Prime or API Tap Water Conditioner. This is the fastest and safest method because it also neutralizes chloramines and heavy metals instantly.
  • Off-gassing: Leave your water in an open-top bucket for 24 hours. The chlorine will naturally evaporate into the air. Note: This does not work for chloramines, which many modern municipal water systems use.
  • Boiling: Boil the water for about 15–20 minutes to accelerate the evaporation process. Ensure the water cools completely to room temperature before adding it to your tank.

Since you are in the Ames area, would you like me to check if your local utility uses chloramines so you know if off-gassing is a safe option?
